kempeYear.say: Alfred Kempe published his proof in 1879.
kempeYear.source: A. B. Kempe, On the Geographical Problem of the Four Colours, American Journal of Mathematics 2 (1879) 193-200

heawoodYear.say: Percy Heawood found the hole in 1890, eleven years later.
heawoodYear.source: P. J. Heawood, Map-colour theorem, Quarterly Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics 24 (1890) 332-338

yearsUnnoticed.say: Kempe's proof stood for eleven years.

erreraGraph.say: Errera's 1921 graph (17 regions) breaks Kempe's whole method, not just one step.

smallestKempeCounterexample.say: The smallest graphs where Kempe's swaps tangle have 9 regions (Soifer 1997, Fritsch 1998).
smallestKempeCounterexample.source: Gethner and Springer, How False Is Kempe's Proof of the Four Color Theorem?, Congressus Numerantium 164 (2003); https://mathworld.wolfram.com/SoiferGraph.html

heawoodFiveColor.say: Heawood rescued Kempe's chains to prove five colors always suffice.

appelHaken.say: The four color theorem was finally proved in 1976 by Appel and Haken, with a computer.
appelHaken.source: K. Appel, W. Haken, Every planar map is four colorable, Illinois J. Math 21 (1977); announced 1976

heawood3col.value: a triangulated map is 3-colorable exactly when every region has an even number of neighbors
heawood3col.say: If three regions meet at every corner, three inks are enough exactly when every region has an even number of neighbors.
heawood3col.source: Heawood 1898 (Quart. J. Pure Appl. Math. 29); checked on every random map in our run

newsHook.value: University of Copenhagen + DTU press release 2026-11-17: a fast four-coloring algorithm (an algorithm, not a new proof)
newsHook.say: This week a Danish team announced a fast way to actually find a four-coloring.
newsHook.source: CONTRACT.md (press release 2026-11-17); verify wording and authors against the release before voicing

fourCornersNotAdjacent.say: Utah-Colorado-Arizona-New Mexico meet at one point; touching at a point does not count, so Arizona and Colorado may share an ink.

statesNeedFour.say: The US map cannot be done with three inks.
statesNeedFour.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/analysis.py: SAT says no 3-coloring exists; obstruction checked by brute force

statesObstruction.say: Nevada and its five neighbors: Oregon, Idaho, Utah, Arizona, California form a ring of five around it. An odd ring needs three inks by itself, and Nevada touches all of them, so it needs a fourth.
statesObstruction.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/analysis.py: smallest odd wheel, all 3^6 = 729 colorings tried, none works

statesNoK4.say: No four states all touch each other; the smallest reason is an odd ring (6 states).

statesOddRingHubs.say: Nevada and West Virginia have rings of 5 neighbors, Kentucky a ring of 7: each one alone forces a fourth ink.

statesMax.say: Missouri and Tennessee touch eight states each, the most.

statesWith5OrFewer.say: 36 of the 49 have five or fewer neighbors.

statesMinNeighbours.say: Maine touches only one state (New Hampshire).

greedy3StuckAt.say: Painting west to east with three inks, it is stuck at Idaho after only 4 states: Washington, Oregon and Nevada already use all three.

search3Backtracks.say: A careful search on Nevada's ring dies in every branch: 9 backtracks and no way to do it with three.

search3WholeMap.say: Searching the whole map with three inks: 35 backtracks, then proof there is no way.
search3WholeMap.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/analysis.py (DSATUR order, first ink fixed)

greedy4StuckAt.say: Even with four inks, painting west to east without thinking gets stuck at Kentucky: Missouri, Illinois, Indiana and Tennessee already use all four. Four is enough, but not if you paint greedily.

kempeStates.say: Kempe's method on the US map: 47 states come back with an ink free, 2 need one chain swap; his flawed step never comes up.

countiesObstruction.say: Catoosa, Walker and Whitfield in Georgia and Hamilton in Tennessee all touch each other: four counties, four inks, no way around it.
countiesObstruction.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/analysis.py: 4-clique; SAT confirms no 3-coloring

countiesK4Count.say: 23 sets of four counties that all touch each other.

countiesMax.say: The county with the most neighbors touches 13.

countiesNotPlanarGraph.say: As a network the county map is not even flat, because some counties come in several pieces; still four inks do it.

worldK4.say: Belgium, France, Germany and Luxembourg all touch each other, so Europe needs four inks.
worldK4.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/analysis.py: 4-clique, brute force + SAT

worldFourWithExclaves.say: Even if every piece of a country must wear the same ink (Kaliningrad with Russia, Nakhchivan with Azerbaijan, Cabinda with Angola, Alaska with the US, French Guiana with France), the real world map still needs only four.
worldFourWithExclaves.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/analysis.py: SAT 4-coloring found and checked edge by edge

worldNotPlanarWithExclaves.say: With exclaves glued to their countries, the world's border network is no longer a flat map, so the theorem does not even promise four. It happens to work anyway.
worldNotPlanarWithExclaves.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/analysis.py (networkx planarity + Kuratowski subgraph)

worldExclaves.say: Neighbours that exist only through an exclave: Russia-Poland and Russia-Lithuania (Kaliningrad), Azerbaijan-Turkey (Nakhchivan), Angola-Congo (Cabinda), France-Brazil and France-Suriname (French Guiana), UK-Ireland (Northern Ireland).
worldExclaves.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/analysis.py world_parts (non-largest part with a land border)

worldMaxNeighbours.say: China touches 17 countries in this data.

worldPointContacts.say: Botswana and Zambia meet at a point (Kazungula); in this data so do Namibia and Zimbabwe.
worldPointContacts.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/maps.py world (points); the real Botswana-Zambia contact is about 150 m of river

kempeFailMap.say: On this nine-region map Kempe's two swaps are each legal, but done together they leave two neighbors on the same ink.
kempeFailMap.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/samples.py find_kempe_fail, verified by verify_kempe.py (independent networkx code)

kempeFixFlips.say: Done one swap at a time and re-checked, 2 swaps free an ink and the map is fine.

randomSizes.say: From 8 to 600 regions each, plus the sea.

randomChromatic.say: 999,510 of them need exactly four inks; only 490 manage with three; none needs five.

randomGreedy.say: Greedy west to east needed a fifth ink on 885,341 maps (88.53%).

kempeClashMaps.say: Kempe's exact procedure (fewest-neighbor region first) hit his broken step and failed on 454,140 of 1,000,000 maps (45.41%).

kempeHardMaps.say: His risky double swap was needed at all on 49.97% of maps.

kempeClashPerDoubleSwap.say: When he needed the double swap, it went wrong 53% of the time.
kempeClashPerDoubleSwap.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/run_random.py, rule mindeg (clash events / double swaps)

kempeClashMapsFirstRule.say: Removing the first eligible region instead of the smallest, it fails on 62.59% of maps.

kempeClashBySize.say: Small maps almost never trip it; big maps almost always do.
kempeClashBySize.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/run_random.py by_size (maps, maps with a clash)

eulerFiveNeighbours.say: Every one of the 1,000,000 maps had a region with five or fewer neighbors, as Euler's formula guarantees (in fact always one with four or fewer).
eulerFiveNeighbours.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/run_random.py (fewest neighbors per map; regions with <= 5 per map)

kempeSequentialFail.say: Even done carefully one swap after the other, in either order, his step leaves the region blocked on 24.86% of maps.
kempeSequentialFail.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/run_random.py, rule mindeg, side check per double swap

kempeSmallMapsSafe.say: On maps of 8 to 15 regions his flawed step never even came up.
kempeSmallMapsSafe.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/run_random.py by_size 8-15, rule mindeg

kempeBigMapsFail.say: On maps of 256 to 600 regions it failed on 198,298 of 198,440.
kempeBigMapsFail.source: our run: sims/fourcolor/run_random.py by_size 256-600, rule mindeg

kempeFanChoice.say: Our one free choice (how the hole is filled) moves the failure rate by a few points, not the picture.
